statement: Whenever count_good_nodes(edges) returns a result r, r equals the number of good nodes, defined as follows. Two vertices u,v are adjacent if some edge has endpoints u and v in either order. Because the graph is a tree rooted at 0, for each vertex v != 0 there is a unique neighbor parent(v) on the unique simple path from 0 to v; children(u) = {v : parent(v)=u}. For any vertex u, subtree(u) is the set of vertices w whose unique simple path from 0 to w contains u, and size(u) = card(subtree(u)). A vertex u is good iff for all c1,c2 in children(u), size(c1)=size(c2); equivalently, u has at most one child, or all its children have the same subtree size.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges)+1. The input satisfies: 2 <= n <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(edges), len(edges[i]) = 2; writing edges[i] = [a_i,b_i] as integers, 0 <= a_i < n, 0 <= b_i < n, and a_i != b_i; the undirected graph with vertex set {0,...,n-1} and edge set {{a_i,b_i} : 0 <= i < len(edges)} is a tree (connected and acyclic).
